title: Commercially safe object detection models for Raspberry Pi 5
dek: On a Raspberry Pi 5, RF-DETR-M (Apache-2.0) reaches 57.4 mAP at 0.8 FPS, ahead of the AGPL-3.0 YOLO26-X at 56.5 mAP and 0.4 FPS.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: On the Raspberry Pi 5, permissive models match the restricted ones on accuracy and, from the small class up, run at least as fast. RF-DETR-M (Apache-2.0) reaches 57.4 mAP at 0.8 FPS against YOLO26-X (AGPL-3.0) at 56.5 mAP and 0.4 FPS. RF-DETR-N lands within 0.9 points of YOLO11-L, YOLOv8-L and YOLO-NAS-S at 2.1 FPS, against 0.9 FPS or less. Only at the nano end do YOLO26-N and YOLO11-N keep a speed lead.

License terms decide whether a model can ship in a closed commercial product. YOLO-NAS carries a non-permissive license from its authors. The Ultralytics models (YOLOv5u, YOLOv8, YOLO11, YOLO26) ship under AGPL-3.0, a copyleft license with source-release obligations. MIT and Apache-2.0 carry no such obligation. This guide covers 22 restricted models and 48 permissive ones on the same Raspberry Pi 5 protocol in PyTorch FP32. mAP is shown in percent form throughout.
This is not legal advice. License names come from each model's upstream repository. Confirm the exact terms with the upstream project and your own counsel before you ship.

RF-DETR-M is 0.9 points ahead of YOLO26-X and runs at twice its frame rate, 0.8 vs 0.4 FPS. RF-DETR-S reaches 55.1 mAP at 1.0 FPS against YOLO-NAS-M at 55.4 and 0.5 FPS. D-FINE-S reaches 53.4 mAP at 1.1 FPS. YOLO26-L sits 0.4 points higher at 0.7 FPS, and YOLO11-X reaches 53.6 at 0.4 FPS.
Medium: RF-DETR-N covers six restricted models

RF-DETR-N reaches 51.4 mAP at 2.1 FPS. YOLO11-L reaches 52.3 at 0.7 FPS, YOLOv8-L 52.0 at 0.6, YOLOv5lu 51.5 at 0.6, and YOLO-NAS-S 51.8 at 0.9. It is also 0.8 points ahead of YOLO11-M and 2.0 ahead of YOLOv8-M, which run 0.9 and 1.1 FPS. On this board the Apache-2.0 pick is the faster one by a wide margin.
Small and nano: close, with one speed gap

DEIMv2-N reaches 46.7 mAP at 2.4 FPS, against YOLO26-S at 47.4 and YOLO11-S at 45.7, both at 2.3 FPS. At the nano end YOLOv9-T (MIT) is 1.3 points ahead of YOLO26-N but runs 2.9 vs 5.0 FPS. PicoDet-M matches YOLOv8-N at 37.6 vs 36.7 mAP and 5.0 vs 5.3 FPS. DEIMv2-Femto beats YOLOv5nu on both axes: 34.5 vs 33.8 mAP at 7.4 vs 5.4 FPS.
The permissive leaderboard on the Raspberry Pi 5

The permissive field runs past every restricted model at the top. DEIMv2-X leads at 61.3 mAP, then ECDet-X at 61.1, both at 0.3 FPS on this board. The table lists the permissive models with verified rows, sorted by accuracy.
